doc.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29

title: Why pianists were called Professor
summary: A question on the term Professor is answered: pianists in Storyville sporting houses were so named; the rest is murmur.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Somebody said they don't dance now, they choose upsides. Yeah, right, man. That's up, man. You said there is one thing I'd like to ask. Where does the word professor come from, for the guy who played the piano? No, I don't know the guy that plays the piano. Yeah, ordinarily they were called professor something.
Do you know where that came from? Well the fellows used to play pianos in the old sporting houses in Storyville. They were always professor somebody, right? Yeah.
The district. They were called, just like the nickname for them, that's all. Yeah, I see. Yeah.

That's my honest thing, you used props, professor, professor, professor. You knew them kind of things. Yeah. It's like you used the word kid. Kid. Tell them how you learned trombone, Jim. That's a good word. Yeah. Yeah.
